summary: Direct x86_64 machine instructions, hardware CPU registers, stack pointers, and system call execution.

rows.means: copies data between CPU registers or between memory and registers
rows.consequence: x86_64 cannot move directly from memory to memory in a single instruction; data must load into a register first.

rows.code: ADD dst, src and SUB dst, src
rows.means: performs arithmetic addition and subtraction on registers
rows.consequence: Updates CPU condition flags (Zero Flag ZF, Carry Flag CF, Sign Flag SF, Overflow Flag OF).

rows.means: compares two operands by computing (op1 - op2) without saving result
rows.consequence: Sets CPU flags based on the subtraction result, immediately followed by conditional jump instructions.

rows.means: unconditional jump: changes instruction pointer (RIP) to target address
rows.consequence: Direct hardware jump instruction, the assembly equivalent of goto.

rows.means: jump if equal (Zero Flag = 1) / jump if not equal
rows.consequence: Conditional branch instructions used to implement if/else statements and loop termination checks.

rows.means: calls subroutine / returns to caller address
rows.consequence: CALL pushes the next instruction address onto the stack; RET pops that address off the stack back into RIP.

rows.means: pushes value onto stack (decrements RSP) / pops into register (increments RSP)
rows.consequence: The x86_64 stack grows downward from high memory to low memory.

rows.means: 64-bit / 32-bit accumulator register; stores function return values
rows.consequence: By calling convention, functions return their numeric or pointer result in RAX.

rows.means: points to the top of the current thread execution stack
rows.consequence: Modified automatically by PUSH, POP, CALL, and RET, or adjusted manually via sub rsp, 32 to allocate local stack frames.

rows.means: frame pointer pointing to the base of current stack frame
rows.consequence: Historically used to index function local variables and arguments; modern compilers often omit it (-fomit-frame-pointer).

rows.code: RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9
rows.means: System V AMD64 ABI registers holding function arguments
rows.consequence: On Linux/macOS, the first 6 integer/pointer arguments to a function are passed in these registers, not on the stack.

rows.means: register holding the memory address of the next instruction to execute
rows.consequence: Cannot be written directly with MOV; updated via jumps, calls, and returns.

rows.means: Load Effective Address: computes address calculation without memory access
rows.consequence: Commonly abused as a fast arithmetic trick: lea rax, [rdi + rsi*4 + 8] performs multiply and add in a single CPU clock cycle.

rows.means: switches from user space (Ring 3) to OS kernel space (Ring 0)
rows.consequence: Passes syscall number in RAX (e.g. 1 for sys_write on Linux) and arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX; invokes OS kernel services.

rows.means: No Operation: advances instruction pointer by 1 byte without doing anything
rows.consequence: Used for memory alignment of loop targets so instructions line up on 16-byte CPU cache line boundaries.
